review: The touch function row looks cool but I keep hitting it by accident and miss physical keys.
Gorgeous design, the glass palm rest and slim bezels make it look very premium.
Keyboard is edge to edge and nice to type on once you get used to the flat keys.
The OLED display is stunning, colours pop and text is razor sharp.
The invisible haptic trackpad is hard to use, I can't feel where it starts and ends.
Only two USB-C ports and no headphone jack, which is a strange choice for a work laptop.
Battery easily lasts a full workday of documents and browsing.
It gets warm under load and the fan becomes noticeable during video calls.
The screen is glossy and quite reflective near windows.
Lovely machine overall, but the missing headphone jack still annoys me.
Too expensive for what you get, similar specs are much cheaper elsewhere.
Battery drops quickly with the OLED at full brightness.
Dell support was quick to arrange a home visit for a loose key.
Webcam is average, fine for meetings but nothing special.
Very compact and light, fits in any bag. Great for travel.
Build quality is excellent, the aluminium chassis feels rock solid.
Performance is snappy for office work and light photo editing.
